Question: Students Arn, Bob, Cyd, Dan, Eve, and Fon are arranged in that order in a circle. They start counting: Arn first, then Bob, and so forth. When the number contains a \(7\) as a digit (such as \(47\)) or is a multiple of \(7\) that person leaves the circle and the counting continues. Who is the last one present in the circle?
Solution:
Keep the counting numbers going after each departure, but skip the people who have left. The first six numbers go to Arn through Fon, so Arn says \(7\) and leaves.

Continue from Bob at \(8\). The departures are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l}
\text{Number}&\text{Person leaving}&\text{People still present}\\\hline
7&\text{Arn}&\text{Bob, Cyd, Dan, Eve, Fon}\\
14&\text{Cyd}&\text{Bob, Dan, Eve, Fon}\\
17&\text{Fon}&\text{Bob, Dan, Eve}\\
21&\text{Bob}&\text{Dan, Eve}\\
27&\text{Eve}&\text{Dan}
\end{array}
\]

For example, after Cyd leaves at \(14\), Dan says \(15\), Eve says \(16\), and Fon says \(17\), which contains a \(7\). After Bob leaves at \(21\), Dan and Eve alternate through \(22,23,24,25,26,27\), so Eve leaves next.

The last person is \(\boxed{\text{Dan}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). Updating the active circle after each departure is essential; the counting numbers themselves never restart.
